learningObjective: Distinguish an event that was available by prediction time from a late-arriving event whose event timestamp alone makes it look eligible.
mediumRationale: An original, phone-width explanatory drawing keeps the complete comparison visible without panning. A topic-specific timeline, quantity, evidence gate, or state relation replaces the component inventory. Geometry, direct labels, accessible descriptions, theme tokens, and static output carry the explanation without interaction.

pages.insight: The data-inspection checklist emphasizes label noise, bias, and inspecting examples, but does not define temporal eligibility.
The experimentation checklist stresses trustworthy training and evaluation skeletons and full test-set evaluation.
The experimentation slide separates offline ground-truth metrics from online production metrics, motivating parity between historical data and serving conditions.
The production checklist explicitly asks about out-of-time test data, feature freshness, and target leakage.
The data-pipeline slide asks how often new data arrives and how raw data becomes model features.
The serving slide covers online updates, monitoring, and inference constraints but does not visualize historical availability.

implementation.accessibility: The Monday-noon cutoff divides knowable evidence from the future. Payment A occurs Monday at 09:00 and is available at 09:05. Payment B occurs at 10:00 but is unavailable until Wednesday. Its early event timestamp cannot authorize using its later-arriving information. All labels use at least 12 viewBox units in a 360-unit-wide composition. Meaning is also encoded by positions, words, line styles, and numbers, not color alone.
